front.title: Benchmarking Methodology for BGP Monitoring Protocol (BMP) Convergence and Scaling

abstract.t: The BGP Monitoring Protocol (BMP) is widely used by operators to stream BGP routing state from routers to monitoring and automation systems. Although BGP convergence has well-established benchmarking methodologies, there is no standardized way to measure how quickly and how completely a router exports BGP state over BMP, or how the BMP export affects the router and the collector. This document defines terminology, a reference test setup, metrics, and test procedures to benchmark the BMP convergence of a router (the Device Under Test) in a vendor-independent and repeatable way. It covers all five BMP monitoring views (Adj-RIB-In pre-policy and post-policy, Loc-RIB, and Adj-RIB-Out pre-policy and post-policy), initial table dump speed, convergence during routing events and churn, impact on BGP itself, scaling with the number of monitored views, the Adj-RIB- Out scale, and BMP stations, and behavior under TCP backpressure.
